module.title: MHD with embedded particle-in-cell regions: FLEKS coupled to the magnetosphere (MHD-AEPIC) and to the outer heliosphere as a test-particle and neutral-fluid model
module.expensive_path: FLEKS is a C++17 semi-implicit (Gauss-law-satisfying energy-conserving) particle-in-cell code on AMReX grids: every PC step gathers fields to millions of macro-particles, pushes them, deposits moments and solves the implicit field equations with a Krylov solver; in the coupled runs GM supplies the initial and boundary state through CON_couple_gm_pc at each coupling and receives the PIC moments back, and the OH+PT tests run FLEKS as test particles or neutral fluids on the OH solution; the particle loops and the field solve dominate PC_run, the AMR regridding of the PIC region (test17 adapt, test23, test25) is the framework-side cost
module.rationale: the embedded PIC coupling is the framework's most distinctive capability (MHD-EPIC and MHD-AEPIC) and FLEKS is one code used in two slots; both coupling directions (GM-PC, OH-PT) share the FLEKS wrapper and the AMReX build, so they are one module with eleven tests; splitting the three OH+PT tests off would leave them thin
excluded: PT/AMPS (not packaged) and PT/MITTENS (swmf-sep-transport) in the same PT slot
the BATSRUS side of the fast-wave and reconnection setups (code/batsrus)
hazards: AMReX is not in the tree: Config.pl clones SWMFsoftware/AMREX (55 MB) into util/AMREX and builds it (make -j 4; make install) on first use, 2-D and 3-D as separate installs; the source PR must vendor it at a pin and the Docker build must run that step; HYPRE is optional
C++ with MPI; the build was not attempted here
the PIC checks compare at 1e-7 to 1e-12 relative, so any change in particle ordering or reduction order shows; deterministic only with a fixed random seed and fixed rank count
test17 runs four SWMF.exe invocations (start, restart, adapt) and test21 and test22 have _4neu and _oh_pt variants each
